text:
Sam: Quick sync — I want to prep a grooming session for a long-term traffic governance roadmap (Q3/Q4). Goals: define isolation lanes, SLA tiers, regional residency controls, and clear launch gates. Anyone got must-have constraints from infra or customers?

Maya: +1. Need to see cost impact per lane. Customers are asking for region pinning and hard residency for PHI — that affects Dedicated vs Shared.

Jin: Technical constraints: cross-region p99 will depend on edge routing and model sharding. Proposal sketch: three lanes — shared (best-effort, cheaper), tenant-isolated (soft isolation + KV partitioning), and dedicated (per-tenant GPU pool). Each lane maps to a routing policy, fallback chain, and telemetry set.

Alex: For launch gates I want concrete acceptance criteria. Suggest: 
- Canary at 5% traffic for 24h with perf and error monitoring
- SLA targets per lane (example: dedicated p99 < 120ms, tenant-isolated p99 < 220ms, shared p99 < 350ms)
- Rollback triggers: +50% error rate, +2x latency p99 vs baseline, or quality regression on evaluation prompts.

Lisa: Sales input — customers will need contractual region residency and audit logs. Also pricing tiers must be clear: committed capacity vs metered. If we split lanes we need clear billing mapping.

Maya: Cost model note — isolated lanes increase steady-state GPU cost by ~30-60% depending on utilization. We should include a measurement plan: sample workloads, project token/sec, simulate KV hits to estimate delta.

Jin: Ops requirements: autoscaling policies must be lane-aware, and routing needs to support per-tenant affinity and a fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained. Also add a safe-eviction policy for noisy tenants.

Sam: Draft agenda for grooming doc: 1) lane definitions + examples, 2) SLA matrix + metrics to collect, 3) launch gates + rollback triggers, 4) billing mapping, 5) migration path for existing tenants. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/traffic-governance (draft). Please add comments by EOD Tuesday. :eyes:

Alex: Tiny ask — add a section for eval-driven quality thresholds. Can't ship lanes that degrade embedding/response quality without explicit customer opt-in.

ops-bot: Reminder: infra capacity planning ticket created — #INC-4821. Autoscaler sizing draft due next week.

Sam: Action items: Jin to produce lane perf estimates, Maya to run a cost sim for 3 sample tenants, Alex to draft launch gate checklist, Lisa to consolidate top 3 customer residency asks. Sync Wednesday 10am. :thumbsup:
